question.prompt:
Circles with centers \(A\) and \(B\) have radii \(3\) and \(8,\) respectively. A common internal tangent intersects the circles at \(C\) and \(D,\) respectively. Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at \(E,\) and \(AE = 5.\) What is \(CD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_12A_Q16_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Drawing the radii to the tangency points creates two right triangles whose sizes can be compared. A radius is perpendicular to a tangent at the point of contact, so \(AC\perp CD\) and \(BD\perp CD\).

An internal tangent puts the centers on opposite sides of the tangent, so \(E\) lies between \(A\) and \(B\). The parallel perpendicular segments \(AC\) and \(BD\) then put \(C\) and \(D\) on opposite rays from \(E\).

In right triangle \(ACE\), the hypotenuse is \(AE=5\) and one leg is \(AC=3\). Thus
\[
EC=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4.
\]
Triangles \(ACE\) and \(BDE\) have right angles at \(C\) and \(D\), and their angles at \(E\) are equal vertical angles. They are therefore similar. Corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{ED}{EC}=\frac{BD}{AC}=\frac{8}{3},
\qquad ED=\frac{32}{3}.
\]
Since \(E\) is between \(C\) and \(D\),
\[
CD=EC+ED=4+\frac{32}{3}=\boxed{\frac{44}{3}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Tangent radii and similar triangles
